guide.title: First aid and safe transport
guide.intro: Read this before going available. It takes about 5 minutes. Your safety comes first.
guide.s1: Park away from traffic, switch on hazard lights, and look for fire, fuel, live wires or fast traffic before you go near. Call 108 if no one has.
guide.s2: If the person fell from a height, was hit by a vehicle, or has neck or back pain, numbness or cannot move their legs, a spine injury is possible. Do not move them unless there is immediate danger (fire, traffic). Wait for the ambulance and keep their head still.
guide.s3: Use several people. Support the head and neck and keep the head, neck and back in a straight line. Move them as one unit, gently, without twisting.
guide.s4: Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth and keep pressing. Do not remove objects stuck in a wound. Raise a bleeding arm or leg if it does not hurt.
guide.s5: If there is no spine injury risk, turn them on their side (recovery position) so they don't choke. Keep checking their breathing. Do not give food or water.
guide.s6: A person who is unconscious or badly hurt should lie flat — a car (4-wheeler) is better. Drive carefully: a crash on the way helps no one. Keep the 108 line open if you can.
guide.s7: Go to the emergency entrance. Tell the staff what happened and what you saw. You can leave after handing over.
guide.law: India's Good Samaritan law (Motor Vehicles Act, Section 134A) protects people who help accident victims in good faith. You are not liable for any injury or death, you do not have to give your name or phone number at the hospital, and you cannot be forced to be a witness. Hospitals cannot ask you to pay or wait.
guide.lawNote: (This is a summary, not legal advice.)
guide.confirm: I have read and understood this guide
guide.done: Thank you. You can now go available.

privacy.title: Privacy and your data
privacy.intro: plusplus follows India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. We collect only what we need to help you.

items.1: Your phone number — to sign you in and to stop fake SOS alerts.
items.2: Your name and emergency contacts — so helpers know who you are and your family gets an SMS if you raise an SOS.
items.3: Your location — only when you use “Near me” or raise an SOS. Responders share theirs only while available.
items.4: Your appointments and what you write about your problem — shared only with the clinic you book.
items.5: Responder and clinic documents — seen only by the plusplus verification team.

privacy.retention: SOS location trails are deleted after 90 days; we keep only anonymous statistics.
privacy.never: We never sell your data and never show a responder's location to the public.
privacy.deleteConfirm: This permanently deletes your account, contacts, appointments and SOS history. This cannot be undone.
